_: NOTES-FROM-PLANNING.md entry 129 section 1.2: every limit shown to the person is the one the receiver
enforces, taken from one place so they cannot drift. The page is built by Python and the receiver is
PHP, and neither can read the other's constants, so this file is the one place and a test holds both
to it. A page that says 30 MB while the receiver refuses at 20 is a page that wastes somebody's
upload and tells them nothing useful about why.
`open` is whether the receiver is installed and answering on the server. While it is false the page is not
built and nothing links to it, because a form that posts to a path the server does not serve is worse than
no form: it takes somebody's photographs, spends their upload and tells them nothing useful. Entry 129's
installer run by Alan is what makes it true.
Entry 173 set it true on 2026-09-24, with the server side of entry 129 finished and the Turnstile secret confirmed present.
The page is at grouplab.org/targets/, and while this is true the top bar's Shoot a target becomes Send a target.
Entry 165 section 2: consent_v2, two levels from one text, shown on the page and by the application alike. testing is used to test
and improve detection and never published; publishable may also be published. A consent_v1 submission stays publishable.
appOpen is whether the application's own receiver, api/app-submission.php, is installed and answering: until it is, the application
never asks anybody to send a target. It is set true by the entry that follows Alan's installing it.
